Lets Lenspilot read what\'s on your screen (button labels, text, layout) so it can highlight where to tap and guide you step by step. Lenspilot only reads the screen — it does not tap, type, or take any action on its own unless you explicitly enable automation.

Lenspilot works both ways:

✅ With Accessibility on, the screen is read directly and quickly (accessibility tree), so guidance appears almost instantly.

➖ With Accessibility off, the app still works, but it must understand the screen through on-device icon detection and text recognition, so it can be a little slower. In that case it needs a one-time screen-capture permission to take screenshots, and the "Display over other apps" permission to draw highlights. These are two separate permissions and do not replace Accessibility.

The whole app can be used without Accessibility; only the speed differs. If you prefer, ignore this for now and continue. You can turn it on or off at any time in Settings.
Turn on Accessibility first, then tap Run again
Accessibility is ON in Settings but still not working

This is usually caused by one of the following:

1) The phone's battery saver has stopped Lenspilot in the background. The service may show ON in Settings while it is not actually running. Tap "Open battery settings" below and set Lenspilot to "No restrictions" / "Unrestricted".

2) Many phones (especially some Chinese brands) have a separate "Auto-launch" / "Startup manager" / "Protected apps" manager outside the normal battery settings. Look for those names (or "App launch") in your phone's Settings. If it exists, turn off "Manage automatically" for Lenspilot and turn ON every toggle (Auto-launch, Run in background and so on). The menu name and location differ by manufacturer, so find the exact steps in your phone's own Settings app.

3) Because this app was installed outside the Play Store, newer Android versions (13+) may block it as a "restricted setting". To fix it: open App Info, tap the ⋮ (three-dot) menu at the top right, tap "Allow restricted settings", then turn Accessibility ON again.

After fixing it, turn Accessibility OFF and ON once more to be certain it works.

📷 Screenshot quality (screen guide, all four models)

The quality of the screenshot the AI uses to choose buttons. Color images do not add tokens but help a great deal in recognizing icons, toggles and enabled/disabled buttons. A higher resolution makes small text and icons clearer (slightly more tokens); a lower one is faster and lighter.
Resolution: very low (~1000px, fastest and lightest)
Resolution: full (actual screen, most accurate, more tokens)
Automatic boost: when the AI says it cannot find something or is unsure, or on an irreversible step (send / delete / payment), that single call sends the full resolution in color
Even with Accessibility on, you can always use the Screen VLM. Without the Accessibility permission, the on-device icon detector model is used (offline, fast).
Accessibility Tree (default; falls back to the on-device icon detector without the permission)
Screen VLM (always, runs on the server, slower but recognizes more icons)
YOLO icon detector (always, runs on the device: offline, fast, fixed icon list)
OCR only (always, reads text only; no icon detection; fastest and cheapest)
Hybrid: YOLO + OCR together (always, runs on the device; combining both gives the strongest and most accurate reading, and may take slightly longer)

This is a regular keyboard, and you type on it just like Google Keyboard. It has one extra ✨ button that, when tapped, uses AI to generate any text and enter it directly into the field (auto-typing).

It does not need the Accessibility permission. It only has to be activated as a keyboard, the same way as any new keyboard app.

In the next step, go to the system settings and turn on "Lenspilot Keyboard", then come back and tap "Switch now".
Lenspilot Keyboard is turned on but is not currently set as the active keyboard. Tap the button below to choose it as the current keyboard.

Lenspilot Keyboard is now on and active ✅\n\nTap any search bar or text field in any app and this keyboard opens. Tap the ✨ button on the keyboard and say or type what you want entered; the AI does the rest.
Find \"Lenspilot Keyboard\" in the list and turn it on

⌨️ Lenspilot Keyboard is now on and active.\n\nTap any search bar or form text field in any app and Lenspilot Keyboard opens. While a task is running, the AI types into the required fields by itself, so you do not need to press anything. You can tap the AI button above to turn this off and type yourself, or tap the stop button in the middle of typing to take control. If the AI cannot tell what to write, it shows a question. Answer it with the microphone button on the control bar instead of the keyboard.
